answer_1.quote: Automated evaluation is crucial for natural language generation tasks, as it measures the performance of related models and consequently promotes the development of NLG research.
answer_1.outputs: Text outputs across nine NLG tasks including summarization, dialogue response generation, data-to-text, paraphrase generation, machine translation, story generation, and text simplification

answer_2.quote: We conducted extensive experiments to evaluate our Themis across six commonly used evaluation datasets for different NLG tasks, including SummEval for summarization, Topical-Chat for dialogue response generation, SFHOT&RES for data-to-text, QAGS for factuality, MANS for story generation, and WMT23 for machine translation (zh-en).

answer_3.quote: Recently, large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and LLaMA have emerged and demonstrated unprecedented performance in instruction following and opendomain generation, which shows great potential for LLM-based automated evaluation to become a new paradigm.

answer_4.quote: we collected 58 evaluation datasets with human annotations across 9 NLG tasks, totaling 0.5 million samples.
answer_4.guideline: The different tasks included in our NLG-Eval corpus and their respective involved evaluation aspects are gathered and shown in Figure, with semantically similar aspects being merged.
